grand_strategy.reading:
The SDF is a case study of a client whose usefulness to a patron was its entire
security. Built by the United States in 2015 as the ground force against ISIS, it
held a quarter of Syria and an oil-and-prison economy without the attributes of a
state: no recognition, no port, no friendly border, an Arab-majority hinterland held
by consent. Luttwak's rule - a patron's help lasts as long as the client serves the
patron's strategy, not its own - played out in three steps: Turkey and the SNA tested
it in December 2024 (Manbij lost, Tishrin and Kobani held with US mediation); the new
Damascus offered integration in March 2025 and the SDF stalled for decentralisation;
and when Syria joined the anti-ISIS coalition in November 2025 the counter-ISIS role
that justified the SDF was duplicated and then disowned. The January 2026 offensive
met no external opposition: the US called for a halt, brokered the terms and, within
three months, left. What remains is a negotiated afterlife: the force dissolved on
25 Aug 2026, its commander is a presidential adviser, Kurdish units survive as
brigades and local security, and the contest has moved from the battlefield to the
constitution. Signals that are not rows: the YPJ is still outside the army, and the
Kobani prison riot of 12 Sep 2026 shows the security vacuum in the Kurdish towns. The
grades in this card are those of an actor that no longer controls territory; read
them as a legacy card with live consequences.

stances.note: The SDF signed the 10 Mar 2025 agreement, lost Raqqa, Deir ez-Zor, the fields and the prisons in January 2026 and announced its own dissolution on 25 Aug 2026; Abdi is now an adviser to the presidency and Kurdish brigades sit inside the army. That is cooperation by necessity, not alignment: Abdi says the struggle for Kurdish rights in the constitution 'will continue', Damascus sidelines the YPJ and pro-SDF Arab units, Kurdish-language education is still negotiated and Kurdish critics call the outcome a surrender. Damascus's own grade of the SDF is `rival` (warming) in the SYR card; the SDF side is `reluctant_partner` because the force has legally merged into the state and no longer seeks to defeat it, but still resists its centralism. No source uses the exact words: the grade is our reading (C), argued from Al Jazeera's 'government terms, Kurdish mistrust' analysis and Abdi's own statements. Bond - grievance: the war of January 2026 and the decade of separation. Evidence mirrored from the SYR card (same links).
